project_specification.overview: Pre-Build Intelligence is a 3-phase pipeline that runs before AutoForge starts building application code. It adds spec validation (Phase 0), architecture planning (Phase 0.5), and dependency auto-detection (enhanced Phase 1) to eliminate wasted agent sessions caused by spec gaps, inconsistent architectural decisions, and missing dependency relationships. This is an internal feature set for the AutoForge codebase.

frontend.state_management: TanStack Query, React hooks and context

backend.database: SQLite with SQLAlchemy (existing registry.db for settings)

communication.api: REST endpoints (FastAPI routers) + WebSocket for real-time updates

prerequisites.environment_setup: - Existing AutoForge development environment (Python 3.11+, Node.js 20+) - AutoForge codebase cloned with all dependencies installed - Familiarity with existing agent types (initializer, coding, testing) - Understanding of existing MCP server pattern (mcp_server/feature_mcp.py) - Understanding of existing orchestrator pattern (parallel_orchestrator.py)

core_features.agent_infrastructure: - CLI accepts new agent types spec-analyzer and architect in --agent-type choices and client.py maps them to empty tool lists, correct max_turns values, and conditionally skips the features MCP server for these agent types - Spec analyzer prompt template exists at .claude/templates/spec_analyzer_prompt.template.md with 6 analysis steps: read spec, completeness analysis, contradiction detection, complexity estimation, dependency risk analysis, and report generation - Architect prompt template exists at .claude/templates/architect_prompt.template.md with 7 design steps: read spec, design database schema, design API structure, map component tree, define routing map, choose patterns and conventions, write ARCHITECTURE.md
core_features.spec_analyzer_agent: - Spec analyzer agent can be invoked via agent.py routing with correct prompt loading from prompts.py and runs as a single-session read-only analysis agent that produces .autoforge/spec-analysis.md - Orchestrator runs spec analyzer as Phase 0 before initialization, parses the completeness score from the generated report, blocks the build if score is below the configurable threshold, and supports --skip-spec-analysis, --min-spec-score (1-5, default 3), and --force-build CLI flags
core_features.architect_agent: - Architect agent can be invoked via agent.py routing with correct prompt loading from prompts.py and runs as a single-session design agent that produces ARCHITECTURE.md in the project root - Orchestrator runs architect as Phase 0.5 after spec analysis and before initialization, verifies ARCHITECTURE.md was created, and CLI supports --skip-architect flag to bypass this phase
core_features.architecture_reference: - Coding prompt template includes ARCHITECTURE.md reading in its orientation step and a mandatory ARCHITECTURE REFERENCE section that instructs coding agents to follow all architectural decisions without deviation - Initializer prompt template includes an instruction to read ARCHITECTURE.md before creating features and use the architecture document for consistent naming, endpoint references, and dependency ordering
core_features.dependency_auto_detection: - Initializer prompt template includes a FIFTH TASK for dependency auto-detection that runs after feature creation, applying heuristic rules to call feature_set_dependencies for each feature based on entity CRUD relationships, auth requirements, and UI composition patterns
core_features.settings_and_api: - Settings API exposes run_spec_analyzer (bool), min_spec_score (int 1-5), run_architect (bool), and force_build (bool) via GET/PATCH on the existing settings endpoint persisted in GlobalSettings, and projects API returns spec_analysis_score and has_architecture fields in the project status response by checking for .autoforge/spec-analysis.md and ARCHITECTURE.md files
core_features.ui_components: - Settings modal includes a Pre-Build Intelligence section with toggles for spec analysis and architecture planning, a slider for minimum spec score, and a checkbox for force build - Project dashboard displays a pipeline status indicator showing completion state of spec analysis (with score badge), architecture planning, initialization, and building phases as a horizontal stepper - Project dashboard includes a collapsible spec analysis report viewer that renders .autoforge/spec-analysis.md as markdown with a colored completeness score badge (red 1-2, yellow 3, green 4-5) and a warning banner when score is below threshold - Project view includes an Architecture tab that renders ARCHITECTURE.md with syntax-highlighted code blocks and a search input for finding specific entities or patterns

tables.note: No new database tables are required. The pre-build intelligence settings are stored in the existing GlobalSettings model in registry.py (SQLAlchemy). New fields added to the existing model: - run_spec_analyzer (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE) - min_spec_score (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 3) - run_architect (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE) - force_build (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE)

api_endpoints_summary.settings: - GET /api/settings (existing - returns all settings including new pre-build fields) - PATCH /api/settings (existing - accepts new pre-build fields for update)
api_endpoints_summary.projects: - GET /api/projects/:name (existing - enhanced response includes spec_analysis_score and has_architecture) - GET /api/projects/:name/spec-analysis (new - returns raw markdown content of .autoforge/spec-analysis.md) - GET /api/projects/:name/architecture (new - returns raw markdown content of ARCHITECTURE.md)

ui_layout.main_structure: - Existing AutoForge UI layout unchanged - New pipeline status indicator added above the kanban board / dependency graph - New spec analysis viewer as collapsible section in project dashboard - New Architecture tab added to project view navigation - New Pre-Build Intelligence section added to Settings modal

design_system.color_palette: - Existing AutoForge neobrutalism design system - Score badge colors: red (#EF4444) for 1-2, yellow (#F59E0B) for 3, green (#10B981) for 4-5 - Pipeline step colors: pending (--color-neo-pending), active (--color-neo-progress), done (--color-neo-done)
design_system.typography: - Existing AutoForge typography system (Inter, system-ui, sans-serif) - Monospace font for code blocks in report/architecture viewers

ui_ux_standards.banned_patterns: - alert(), confirm(), prompt() - Use existing Modal/Toast system - Raw timestamps - Use relative time formatting - Loading spinners without context - Use skeleton loaders with descriptive text
ui_ux_standards.required_components: - Use existing AutoForge UI components (from Radix UI primitives) - Pipeline stepper follows neobrutalism style with bold borders and solid fills - Score badge uses existing badge patterns with color coding
ui_ux_standards.feedback_protocol: - Settings changes: immediate save with toast confirmation - Pipeline phase completion: stepper updates via WebSocket - Build blocked by low score: warning banner with actionable message

coding_standards.architecture: - Follow existing AutoForge patterns: routers in server/routers/, services in server/services/ - Python code must pass ruff check and mypy type checking - TypeScript code must pass npm run lint and npm run build - New prompt templates follow existing fallback chain pattern in prompts.py - Agent routing follows existing pattern in agent.py (if/elif on agent_type) - Orchestrator phases follow existing _run_initializer() subprocess pattern
coding_standards.error_handling: - Spec analyzer failure: log warning, skip phase, proceed with build - Architect failure: log warning, skip phase, proceed without ARCHITECTURE.md - Score parsing failure: default to score 0, respect force_build flag - Missing files: graceful degradation (UI hides sections when files don't exist)

key_interactions.pre_build_pipeline_flow: 1. User starts a build (via UI or CLI) for a project with an app_spec.txt 2. Orchestrator checks if spec analysis is enabled and not already done 3. Phase 0: Spec analyzer agent reads app_spec.txt and writes .autoforge/spec-analysis.md 4. Orchestrator parses completeness score from report 5. If score is below threshold and force_build is off, build is blocked with actionable message 6. If score passes, Phase 0.5: Architect agent reads spec and analysis, writes ARCHITECTURE.md 7. Phase 1: Enhanced initializer creates features, then runs dependency auto-detection second pass 8. Phase 2+: Coding agents proceed as normal, referencing ARCHITECTURE.md for consistency
key_interactions.settings_configuration_flow: 1. User opens Settings modal via gear icon or comma key 2. User scrolls to Pre-Build Intelligence section 3. User toggles spec analysis on/off, adjusts minimum score slider, toggles architecture planning 4. Changes save immediately via PATCH /api/settings with toast confirmation 5. Next build respects the updated settings
key_interactions.spec_analysis_review_flow: 1. After spec analysis completes, pipeline status indicator updates to show score badge 2. User clicks the spec analysis step or expands the report viewer section 3. Report renders as formatted markdown with tables for gaps, contradictions, and risks 4. If score is below threshold, warning banner shows with suggestion to revise spec 5. User can force-build via checkbox in settings or --force-build CLI flag

success_criteria.functionality: - Spec analyzer agent runs as Phase 0 and produces a valid spec-analysis.md with completeness score - Architect agent runs as Phase 0.5 and produces ARCHITECTURE.md with database schema, API structure, component tree, routing map, and conventions - Build is blocked when spec score is below threshold (unless force_build is set) - Initializer second pass detects dependencies using heuristic rules and calls feature_set_dependencies - Coding agents read and follow ARCHITECTURE.md for all architectural decisions - All phases are idempotent (skip if output already exists) - All phases can be individually skipped via CLI flags or settings
success_criteria.user_experience: - Pipeline status indicator clearly shows which phases have completed - Spec analysis report is readable with actionable findings - Architecture document is searchable and well-formatted - Settings controls are intuitive with clear labels and descriptions - Warning banner for low spec score provides clear next steps
success_criteria.technical_quality: - Python code passes ruff check and mypy with no errors - TypeScript code passes npm run lint and npm run build with no errors - New agent types follow existing patterns in client.py and agent.py - Orchestrator phases follow existing subprocess management pattern - No regressions to existing initializer, coding, or testing agent flows - Prompt templates follow existing fallback chain (project-specific then base template)
